The emergy evaluation consists of two separated parts e emergy synthesis of building construction and simulation of operational energy for conditioning. Baseline results in the BES module, see Fig. 4, identify a baseline energy use intensity (EUI) of 0.58 GJ/m2 (161.11 kWh/m2). Office buildings are typically internal load dominated, so interior equipment loads takes the large share of total energy use, 0.21 GJ/m2 (58.33 kWh/m2). Interior and exte rior lighting rank second with an EUI of 0.17 GJ/m2 (47.22 kWh/m2). The loads directly connected to the design scenario are space conditioning (heating and cooling) and interior lighting energy, and they use 0.30 GJ/m2 (82.94 kWh/m2) which represents more than half of the total in relation to the change in perimeter environ mental conditions.

The building energy simulation module is developed to estimate the operational energy use over a building's useful life. The energy calculation results become inputs to the emergy synthesis for Emuse, see Eq. (3). EnergyPlus is used in this module to perform energy simulation to analyze energy demands of individual com ponents. The information that can be entered an EnergyPlus Input Data File (Table 1). Since building form optimization through the integrated energy-emergy assessment is the goal of this research, building geometry, window size, orientation, and building materials become model input variables; see Table 3. Energy use data estimated within the BES module is exported to the BEMA module.
